behaviours.title: A deposit into a new account credits it and records a deposit entry
behaviours.given: a new Ledger with no accounts
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, balance('A') is 100 and entries('A') is one entry { txnId: 't1', kind: 'deposit', amount: 100 }
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is refused because account 'A' was never opened, and balance('A') stays 0
contrary_alternatives: the deposit is accepted but no history entry is recorded

behaviours.title: An unknown account reads as balance 0 with no entries
behaviours.given: a new Ledger where account 'X' has never been used
behaviours.then: balance('X') is 0 and entries('X') is an empty list
behaviours.contrary_then: balance('X') is reported as undefined (no such account) rather than 0
contrary_alternatives: reading an unknown account fails with an error

behaviours.title: Opening an account that already exists does not reset it
behaviours.then: balance('A') stays 100 and its single deposit entry is kept
behaviours.contrary_then: the account is re-created: balance('A') becomes 0 and its history is emptied
contrary_alternatives: open throws an error because the account already exists

behaviours.title: A deposit of 0 is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and balance('A') stays 0 with no entries
behaviours.contrary_then: the zero deposit is accepted ({ ok: true }) and a deposit entry of 0 is recorded
contrary_alternatives: the zero deposit is silently ignored and reported as { ok: true } with nothing recorded

behaviours.title: A negative deposit is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and balance('A') stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the negative deposit is accepted and balance('A') becomes 50
contrary_alternatives: the negative deposit is treated as a deposit of 50 and balance('A') becomes 150

behaviours.title: A deposit amount that is not a number (NaN) is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and balance('A') stays 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is accepted ({ ok: true })
contrary_alternatives: the deposit is accepted and treated as 0

behaviours.title: Repeating a deposit with the same txnId is acknowledged but not applied twice
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, balance('A') stays 100 and there is still only one entry
behaviours.contrary_then: the repeat is applied again and balance('A') becomes 200
contrary_alternatives: the repeat is refused with a duplicate-transaction error
the repeat is applied and a second entry is recorded

behaviours.title: An invalid amount is rejected even when the txnId was already used
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } (the amount check comes before the duplicate check)
behaviours.contrary_then: the call is recognised as a duplicate of 't1' and acknowledged as { ok: true }
contrary_alternatives: the call is rejected with a duplicate-transaction reason

behaviours.title: Deposit amounts are rounded to the nearest cent, with half a cent rounding up
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, balance('A') is 0.13 and the entry amount is 0.13
behaviours.contrary_then: the amount is truncated to 0.12
contrary_alternatives: the amount is kept unrounded at 0.125
the deposit is rejected because it has more than two decimals

behaviours.title: Deposit amounts with a third decimal below 5 round down to the cent
behaviours.then: balance('A') is 1.23
behaviours.contrary_then: the amount is kept as 1.234
contrary_alternatives: the amount is rounded up to 1.24

behaviours.title: A deposit smaller than half a cent is accepted but records an amount of 0
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, balance('A') is 0 and one deposit entry with amount 0 is recorded
behaviours.contrary_then: the deposit is rejected as invalid-amount because it rounds to 0
contrary_alternatives: the deposit is kept unrounded and balance('A') becomes 0.004

behaviours.title: Withdrawing exactly the whole balance is allowed
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and balance('A') becomes 0, with a withdrawal entry of 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is rejected as insufficient-funds and balance('A') stays 100
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is rejected because a minimum balance must remain

behaviours.title: Withdrawing one cent more than the balance is rejected
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' } and balance('A') stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is accepted ({ ok: true }) and balance('A') becomes -0.01
contrary_alternatives: only the available 100 is withdrawn and balance('A') becomes 0

behaviours.title: Withdrawing more than the balance is rejected and the balance is unchanged
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' } and balance('A') stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is accepted and balance('A') becomes -50
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is partially filled and balance('A') becomes 0

behaviours.title: Withdrawing from an account that was never funded is rejected as insufficient-funds
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' } and balance('Z') is 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is rejected with reason 'unknown-account'
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is accepted and balance('Z') becomes -10

behaviours.title: A withdrawal of 0 is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and no withdrawal entry is recorded
behaviours.contrary_then: the zero withdrawal is accepted ({ ok: true }) and recorded as a withdrawal entry of 0
contrary_alternatives: the zero withdrawal is silently acknowledged as { ok: true } with nothing recorded

behaviours.title: A negative withdrawal is rejected rather than acting as a deposit
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and balance('A') stays 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the negative withdrawal is accepted and balance('A') becomes 110
contrary_alternatives: the negative withdrawal is treated as a withdrawal of 10 and balance('A') becomes 90

behaviours.title: Repeating a withdrawal with the same txnId is acknowledged but not applied twice
behaviours.given: account 'A' held 100 and withdraw('A', 30, 'w1') has succeeded (balance 70)
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and balance('A') stays 70 with two entries in total
behaviours.contrary_then: the repeat is applied again and balance('A') becomes 40
contrary_alternatives: the repeat is refused with a duplicate-transaction error

behaviours.title: A txnId already used by a deposit makes a withdrawal with that txnId a silent no-op
behaviours.when: withdraw('A', 40, 't1') is called with the same txnId
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } but balance('A') stays 100 and no withdrawal entry is recorded
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is applied because it is a different kind of operation, and balance('A') becomes 60
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is refused with a duplicate-transaction error

behaviours.title: A rejected withdrawal does not use up its txnId, so it can be retried later
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 50 and withdraw('A', 100, 'w1') was rejected for insufficient-funds, then deposit('A', 50, 'd2') brought the balance to 100
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and balance('A') becomes 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the retry is treated as a duplicate of the rejected 'w1', acknowledged, and balance('A') stays 100
contrary_alternatives: the retry is refused because the txnId was already used

behaviours.title: Withdrawing exactly the daily limit of 5000 in one go is allowed
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 10000 and has not withdrawn anything
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and balance('A') becomes 5000
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is rejected with reason 'daily-limit' and balance('A') stays 10000
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is capped and only part of it is paid out

behaviours.title: Withdrawing one cent over the daily limit of 5000 is rejected
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 10000 and has not withdrawn anything
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'daily-limit' } and balance('A') stays 10000
behaviours.contrary_then: the withdrawal is accepted ({ ok: true }) and balance('A') becomes 4999.99
contrary_alternatives: only 5000 is paid out and balance('A') becomes 5000

behaviours.title: The daily limit is cumulative across withdrawals on the same account
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 10000 and has already withdrawn 3000 and then 2000 (5000 in total)
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'daily-limit' } and balance('A') stays 5000
behaviours.contrary_then: each withdrawal is checked on its own, so the 0.01 is accepted ({ ok: true })
contrary_alternatives: the 0.01 is refused as insufficient-funds

behaviours.title: A withdrawal rejected by the daily limit does not count toward the limit
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 10000, withdrew 4000, then had withdraw 2000 rejected for daily-limit
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and balance('A') becomes 5000
behaviours.contrary_then: the rejected 2000 is still counted, so the 1000 is rejected with 'daily-limit' and balance('A') stays 6000
contrary_alternatives: the whole account is blocked for the day after the first rejection

behaviours.title: The daily limit is tracked separately per account
behaviours.given: accounts 'A' and 'B' each hold 10000 and 'A' has withdrawn 5000
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true } and balance('B') becomes 5000
behaviours.contrary_then: the limit is shared across the whole ledger, so 'B' is rejected with 'daily-limit'
contrary_alternatives: 'B' is refused because the limit applies to the ledger owner rather than each account

behaviours.title: Insufficient funds is reported before the daily limit when both apply
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' }
behaviours.contrary_then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'daily-limit' }
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is accepted and balance('A') becomes -5900

behaviours.title: Transfers are not subject to or counted toward the daily withdrawal limit
behaviours.then: both succeed: balance('A') becomes 7000 and balance('B') becomes 8000
behaviours.contrary_then: the 8000 transfer is rejected with 'daily-limit'
contrary_alternatives: the transfer succeeds but counts toward the limit, so the 5000 withdrawal is rejected with 'daily-limit'

behaviours.title: A withdrawal amount is rounded to cents before the balance check
behaviours.then: the amount rounds to 1, the result is { ok: true } and balance('A') becomes 0
behaviours.contrary_then: the unrounded 0.999 is withdrawn, leaving balance('A') at 0.001
contrary_alternatives: the withdrawal is rejected as insufficient-funds

behaviours.title: A transfer moves money between accounts and records an entry on each side
behaviours.given: account 'A' holds 100 and 'B' has never been used
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, balance('A') is 60, balance('B') is 40, 'A' gets a transfer-out entry of 40 and 'B' gets a transfer-in entry of 40
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer is refused because 'B' was never opened, and balance('A') stays 100
contrary_alternatives: the transfer succeeds but only a single entry is recorded on 'A'

behaviours.title: Transferring exactly the whole balance is allowed
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, balance('A') is 0 and balance('B') is 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer is rejected as insufficient-funds and both balances stay as they were
contrary_alternatives: the transfer is rejected because a minimum balance must remain in 'A'

behaviours.title: Transferring one cent more than the balance is rejected and nothing moves
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'insufficient-funds' }, balance('A') stays 100, balance('B') stays 0 and no transfer entries are recorded
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer goes through ({ ok: true }), balance('A') becomes -0.01 and balance('B') becomes 100.01
contrary_alternatives: only the available 100 is transferred

behaviours.title: A transfer of 0 is rejected as invalid-amount
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and no entries are recorded for 'B'
behaviours.contrary_then: the zero transfer is accepted ({ ok: true })
contrary_alternatives: the zero transfer is silently acknowledged as { ok: true } with nothing recorded

behaviours.title: A negative transfer is rejected rather than moving money backwards
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: false, reason: 'invalid-amount' } and both balances stay 100
behaviours.contrary_then: the transfer is applied in reverse: balance('A') becomes 130 and balance('B') becomes 70
contrary_alternatives: the sign is ignored and 30 moves from 'A' to 'B'

behaviours.title: Repeating a transfer with the same txnId is acknowledged but not applied twice
behaviours.given: account 'A' held 100 and transfer('A', 'B', 40, 't1') has succeeded
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, balance('A') stays 60 and balance('B') stays 40
behaviours.contrary_then: the repeat is applied again: balance('A') becomes 20 and balance('B') becomes 80
contrary_alternatives: the repeat is refused with a duplicate-transaction error

behaviours.title: A transfer from an account to itself is accepted, leaves the balance unchanged and records two entries
behaviours.then: the result is { ok: true }, balance('A') stays 100, and entries('A') gains a transfer-out of 30 then a transfer-in of 30
behaviours.contrary_then: the self-transfer is rejected and entries('A') holds only the original deposit
contrary_alternatives: the self-transfer is acknowledged but records nothing

behaviours.title: Transfer amounts are rounded to the nearest cent, with half a cent rounding up
behaviours.then: balance('B') is 0.13 and the transfer-in entry amount is 0.13
behaviours.contrary_then: the amount is truncated and balance('B') is 0.12
contrary_alternatives: the amount is moved unrounded as 0.125

behaviours.title: The list returned by entries is a copy; changing it does not change the ledger's history
behaviours.when: the caller empties the array returned by entries('A') and reads entries('A') again
behaviours.then: entries('A') still has 1 entry
behaviours.contrary_then: the caller's change leaks into the ledger and entries('A') is now empty
contrary_alternatives: entries returns a frozen list and emptying it throws an error
